samples.summary: Design doc claims "the raw readers clamp again at the point of use", but several raw `listLevel` readers were left unnormalized
samples.evidence: The new section in docs/design/docs/docs.md ("The raw readers clamp again at the point of use, because they are the ones that break rather than merely misrender") is only partly true of the code shipped. Normalized: layout.ts:497/1097, markdown.ts:145, pdf-painter.ts:370/593. Left raw, all multiplying the level into geometry: table-layout.ts:93 (`LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` — the in-cell list indent), paint-layout.ts:198, doc-canvas.ts:599, table-renderer.ts:524, peer-cursor.ts:254 and :392. The two read boundaries (crdt-tree.ts:250, yorkie-doc-store.ts:501) mostly cover these in practice, so the cost is an invariant documented more strongly than it is enforced plus a possible NaN geometry path for blocks that never pass a boundary (e.g. locally-constructed/imported blocks), rather than a user-visible regression.
searchedFor: checked which readers the diff touches (layout, markdown, pdf-painter)

samples.summary: Three near-identical `applyListLevelChanges` write loops instead of one shared applier
samples.evidence: editor.ts:1601-1615, text-editor.ts (private applyListLevelChanges) and text-box-editor.ts:820-835 each repeat the same plan-then-write loop (`planListLevelChanges(...)` then `setBlockType(id, 'list-item', {listKind, listLevel})`), with only editor.ts's markDirty differing. The planner was extracted to one module precisely to avoid drift, but the write half stayed copied three ways; a future change to how a level is written (e.g. also clearing `marker`, or batching internally) has to be made in three places. Behaviour today is correct, so the cost stays inside the codebase.

samples.summary: Clipboard parser still hand-rolls the band clamp the new `normalizeListLevel` owns
samples.evidence: list-level.ts:5 says MAX_LIST_LEVEL "match[es] the clamp the clipboard parser applies", and the diff imports MAX_LIST_LEVEL into clipboard.ts, but clipboard.ts:349-351 keeps its own `Math.min(MAX_LIST_LEVEL, Math.max(0, Math.trunc(level)))`. That is two implementations of one invariant, and they already differ subtly (`Math.trunc` vs the normalizer's `Math.floor`, i.e. -0.5 → 0 both ways today but divergent semantics for negatives before the max). Reusing `normalizeListLevel` would leave a single definition, which is the module's stated purpose.

samples.summary: `walkCellsForSiblings` duplicates `walkCellsForBlock`'s traversal rather than sharing it
samples.evidence: The new `walkCellsForSiblings` (document.ts:96-112) is a byte-for-byte structural clone of `walkCellsForBlock` (just above it) differing only in what it returns. One walker returning the (cellBlocks, block) pair — or `walkCellsForSiblings` implemented on top of the existing one — would keep a single traversal of the nested-table shape; two copies will drift when the table model gains a nesting site.

samples.summary: Unrelated header/footer selection fix bundled into the #1050 change
samples.evidence: `forEachBlockInSelection`'s multi-block branch is switched from `this.doc.document.blocks[i]` to `this.doc.getContextBlocks()[i]` (text-editor.ts:2880-2884). That is a pre-existing bug for header/footer multi-block selections affecting every consumer of the walker (indent/outdent margins, and any other caller), not only list-level carrying, and it arrives with no issue reference of its own. Same for the `recordCursorForHistory` split (#523/#609), though that one is a genuine prerequisite of the new batching. Scope creep with a real fix inside it — worth calling out so the extra behaviour change is reviewed on its own merits.

samples.summary: Design doc says "All six writers route through it" but enumerates seven
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs.md:155-159 lists `handleTab`, `handleIndent`, `handleOutdent` in text-editor.ts (3) plus the `indent`/`outdent` pair in both editor.ts and text-box-editor.ts (4) — seven writers, not six. Nested design docs are not checked by any lane, so nothing else will catch the miscount.

samples.summary: Slides PPTX export keeps its own 0..8 list-level clamp now that a canonical normalizer exists
samples.evidence: `listLevelAttr` (slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:82-86) clamps to the same `[0, 8]` band with its own `Math.trunc`/`Math.min(8, n)` and a hardcoded 8. With `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`/`normalizeListLevel` now exported from `@wafflebase/docs` (both entries), this is a third copy of the band. Not required by the issue and the PPTX ceiling is independently spec-fixed by ST_TextIndentLevelType, hence a nit rather than duplication that must be folded.
